recent_posts.title: Online Password Managers Keep Getting Hacked
Canonical Is Adding AI to Ubuntu
When The AI Model Comes With RCE
recent_posts.summary: A critical unpatched RCE vulnerability has been discovered in SGLang, a popular LLM inference engine powering over 400,000 GPUs worldwide. The attack vector is a malicious GGUF model file containing a crafted tokenizer chat template with a Jinja2 payload. When SGLang's reranking endpoint processes any request, it renders the chat template using an unsandboxed Jinja2 environment, allowing arbitrary Python code execution on the host server. The attacker must first get the victim to load the malicious model — achievable via supply chain attacks or social engineering on model hubs like Hugging Face. Full server compromise, data exfiltration, and lateral movement are possible outcomes. The fix is straightforward: replace the default Jinja2 environment with Jinja2's SandboxedEnvironment, as demonstrated by the already-patched CVE-2024-34359 in llama.cpp.

recent_posts.title: France Is Ditching Windows for Linux
recent_posts.summary: France's central IT agency (DINUM) formally announced on April 8th, 2026 that all government ministries must produce migration plans away from Windows toward Linux by autumn 2026, covering desktops, collaboration tools, AI, databases, and more. This is part of a long-running digital sovereignty push — the national police force (Gendarmerie) has already migrated 103,000 workstations to a custom Ubuntu distro called Gendarmubuntu, saving €2 million per year. France is also developing Securix (a hardened NixOS-based PC model) and La Suite (a self-hosted cloud office suite with video conferencing and spreadsheet tools). Key challenges include legacy Windows applications, compatibility issues, vendor pressure, and the human factor of user training and support. The post argues France's methodical, tiered approach is the right strategy and hopes the blueprint spreads across Europe.

recent_posts.title: How to protect your home router from state-sponsored hacking
recent_posts.summary: FBI and NSA have issued warnings about state-sponsored hacking groups exploiting vulnerable home routers. A specific TP-Link vulnerability allows attackers to bypass authentication via a crafted GET request to the HTTPD service, gaining admin credentials. Once inside, attackers can modify DHCP/DNS settings to hijack all network traffic and perform man-in-the-middle attacks without compromising individual devices. Practical defenses include auditing router settings, disabling remote management, updating firmware, changing default passwords, and checking DNS server configurations. For end-of-life devices, open-source firmware like DD-WRT or OpenWrt is recommended, or building a DIY router with pfSense for stronger security.

recent_posts.title: How to install Arch Linux using the archinstall script
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of archinstall, the official Python-based installer bundled with Arch Linux ISOs. Covers the updated v4.0 textual interface and walks through each configuration step: language/locale, mirror selection, disk partitioning (ext4, LUKS encryption), bootloader choice, kernel selection, user setup, desktop profile (XFCE), audio (PipeWire), firewall (UFW), network config, additional packages (Firefox, Steam via multilib), timezone, and saving the configuration as a reusable JSON file for future deployments. Also discusses the philosophical controversy around archinstall clashing with Arch's DIY ethos.

recent_posts.title: Uncomplicated Firewall Guide
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly walkthrough of UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall) on Linux, covering how to enable it, configure default deny rules, allow common services like SSH, HTTP, and HTTPS, and apply the principle of least privilege. Key topics include avoiding common mistakes like locking yourself out of SSH, using application profiles, creating custom profiles for deployment automation, restricting access by IP address and network interface, and understanding TCP vs UDP protocols.

recent_posts.title: How to download Linux packages anonymously over I2P
recent_posts.summary: A guide to using I2P (Invisible Internet Project) to download and seed Linux distributions and packages anonymously, framed as a response to emerging age verification laws affecting software distribution. Covers torrenting Linux ISOs via I2P's built-in I2PSnark client and configuring qBittorrent to route through I2P using the SAM bridge and HTTP proxy. Also demonstrates setting up a pacman wrapper script on Artix Linux to route package downloads through an I2P mirror (Corey's Artix Mirror), including disabling pacman's download timeout for slow dark web connections. Advocates for Artix Linux specifically because it avoids systemd, which recently merged age verification code into its codebase.

recent_posts.title: How Meta lobbied to shift child safety liability onto Apple and Google
recent_posts.summary: Meta spent $26.3 million on lobbying in 2025, more than any other US company, largely to push the App Store Accountability Act at federal and state levels. Rather than facing potential $50+ billion in COPPA fines for knowingly hosting underage users on Instagram, Meta drafted legislation that shifts age-verification responsibility onto Apple, Google, and other OS/app store providers. Meta also funneled over $70 million through front groups like the Digital Childhood Alliance to obscure its role. Multiple state bills have passed or are pending, while Apple and Google are lobbying against these measures. The piece also notes Meta is dropping end-to-end encryption in Instagram DMs.

recent_posts.title: Age verification laws and their implications for Linux and open source software
recent_posts.summary: A critical look at the App Store Accountability Act and related state-level laws (California, Colorado) that would require age verification for app stores and potentially OS installation. The piece analyzes how such legislation would affect Linux distributions and package managers like apt, Flatpak, and the AUR, noting the 5 million user threshold that might exempt most distros. It argues these laws are primarily about mass surveillance rather than child protection, and suggests that free and open-source software, self-compiled packages, and tools like Portage offer a path to non-compliance for technically savvy users.

top_posts.title: Desktop Linux distributions gain traction as Windows 11 prioritizes AI over performance
top_posts.summary: Windows 11's focus on AI features has degraded gaming performance by up to 65% for Nvidia users, prompting increased adoption of desktop Linux distributions. Zorin OS 18 attracted over 1 million downloads (78% from Windows users) with features like web app integration, Windows app compatibility via Wine, and suggested alternatives for Windows programs. Gaming-focused distributions like Bazzite and CachyOS now match or exceed Windows 11 performance out-of-the-box, while Microsoft's AI-generated code (30% of repos) and financial ties to OpenAI suggest the company won't reverse course on its agentic OS direction.

top_posts.title: Steam OS outperforms Windows 11 in handheld gaming benchmarks
top_posts.summary: Performance testing reveals Linux-based Steam OS consistently outperforms Windows 11 on identical handheld gaming hardware. The Legion Go S running Steam OS achieves higher frame rates in popular AAA games like Cyberpunk 2077 (59 vs 46 FPS) and Witcher 3 (76 vs 66 FPS), despite using Proton compatibility layer to run Windows games. Linux also delivers superior battery life, sometimes more than doubling gaming time compared to Windows. The performance advantage stems from Linux's reduced system overhead versus Windows 11's bloat, including resource-heavy components like React Native-based start menu and integrated ads/AI features.

top_posts.title: Efficient Methods to Learn Linux: Using Arch Wiki, Man Pages, and TLDR
top_posts.summary: The best way to learn Linux is by using the Arch Wiki and man pages for necessary commands. Despite the reputation of Arch Linux as being for advanced users, its automated installer makes it accessible for beginners too. You can also use Manjaro for a GUI-based setup. While YouTube tutorials can be helpful, they often lack the detail and accuracy of written documentation. Moreover, setting up Vim for man pages can enhance your learning experience with syntax highlighting and better navigation features. Tools like TLDR and WikiMan can also simplify learning by providing concise command documentation and offline access to the Arch Wiki.

top_posts.title: Wubuntu faces legal and security issues while mimicking Windows
top_posts.summary: Wubuntu is a new Linux distribution that mimics the look and feel of Windows 11, preloaded with Microsoft and other proprietary software. The distro’s origins trace back to Linux FX, which rebranded due to serious security issues and misleading user data. Wubuntu's legality and security are under question, given the use of visual assets and proprietary software without proper permissions. Users are advised to customize established distributions like Kubuntu instead.

top_posts.title: The YouTube Game Engine
top_posts.summary: Some innovative users have transformed YouTube's caption feature into a functional game engine. By creatively manipulating captions and integrating them into video elements, they have developed interactive games. These games use the capability to move captions around, creating dynamic gameplay scenarios, although it's clear that YouTube's original intent for captions was far from gaming. This creative repurposing shows the potential for new ways to use existing technology.
